question.text: What will be the ending value of the ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread for these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 23 - Dec 4)
question.resolution_criteria: Each subquestion will resolve as the last available daily value of the ICE BofA US High Yield OAS published on the [FRED website](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAMLH0A0HYM2) for the final calendar day (typically the final Friday) of the corresponding biweekly period.
question.fine_print:
* If the FRED data is delayed, the value will be taken as soon as published for the relevant date.
* If the market is closed on the scheduled ending date or if no value for that date is published by FRED for two weeks, the most recent available value from an earlier day in the period will be used.
* Only the initially published value for each date will be used (no revisions).
* The value is reported in percentage points.

# ICE BofA US High Yield OAS: research for the Nov 23 to Dec 4, 2026 period

The spread stood at 3.23 pp on Nov 13, 2026. That is near the middle of the question's 1.745 to 3.745 range. Nothing has happened yet that settles the question.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-13: FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 latest value is **3.23** (daily, not seasonally adjusted). Earlier days: 3.20 on Nov 12, 3.30 on Nov 11, 3.30 on Nov 10, 3.34 on Nov 9. FRED shows the next update on Nov 17. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAMLH0A0HYM2)
- I could not download FRED's own CSV file (the requests timed out). I read the daily values from a mirror of the FRED data instead, generated 2026-11-16, which matches FRED through Nov 12. [govspending CSV](https://govspending.org/api/export/fred/BAMLH0A0HYM2.csv)
- The value that counts is the first one FRED publishes for Friday 2026-12-04.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the outcome. The resolution date is about 14 trading days away.
- 2026-11-13: the spread is 3.23, roughly 0.25 below the cycle's recent peak of 3.48 on Nov 5. [govspending CSV](https://govspending.org/api/export/fred/BAMLH0A0HYM2.csv)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 0.29 pp in a week to about 5.15%, the biggest weekly jump since April 2025. On Nov 13 the semiconductor index fell 3.4% and the Nasdaq fell 0.9%, though the S&P 500 still gained 2.5% for the week. Coming up: Nvidia earnings (Nov 17) and the Fed's meeting minutes. [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/the-tech-selloff-faces-a-credit-test-202611160728) (I could not open this page, error 403; the facts come from the news summary I was given)
- 2026-11-14: Bank of America strategist Michael Hartnett stays defensive. He wants oil below $70, the 10-year yield below 4.5% and a weaker dollar before turning positive on risk assets. [ADVFN](https://investorshub.advfn.com/market-news/article/39985/bank-of-americas-hartnett-maintains-cautious-market-outlook-until-treasury-yields-and-oil-prices-decline)
- About 2026-11-10: Single-B spreads widened 35 bp to 367 bp, their widest since March, driven by bonds tied to AI data centers. The overall HY spread hit 348 bp during a stock selloff, then narrowed to 342 bp. [Globe and Mail](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/article-ai-debt-faces-pressure-as-democrats-prepare-to-take-over-congress/)
- About 2026-11-10: Nuveen put the Bloomberg HY index spread at 336 bp after a week that was positive but turned cautious by Friday. [Nuveen](https://www.nuveen.com/global/insights/fixed-income/fixed-income-weekly-commentary)
- 2026-11-05: A less established outlet reported CCC-rated yields near 18%; treat this with caution. [Whalesbook](https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/economy/US-Junk-Bond-Yields-Hit-18percent-as-Distressed-Debt-Hits-dollar225-Billion/6aecbf8e4fc30694db5fb2ab)
- 2026-10-28: The Fed held rates at 3.75 to 4.00% by a 10-2 vote, after hiking on Sep 16. Reported market odds of a December hike were about 85%. [CTOL](https://www.ctol.digital/news/fed-holds-10-2-vote-treasury-yields-retrace-december-hike/)
- 2026-10-09: CNBC said junk bonds were "flashing yellow". [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/09/junk-bonds-are-flashing-yellow-watch-these-warning-signs.html)

## 4. Base rates
**Path over the last three months** (all from the [govspending CSV](https://govspending.org/api/export/fred/BAMLH0A0HYM2.csv)):
- Late Aug to Sep 22: steady around 2.60 to 2.76; the 52-week low of about 2.66 came around Sep 21.
- Sep 24 to Oct 1: jumped from 2.80 to 3.24.
- October: mostly 3.03 to 3.40, closing the month at 3.44 on Oct 30.
- Nov 5: peak of 3.48.
- Nov 12 to 13: eased back to 3.20 to 3.23.
- Rolling 52-week high was about 3.77 (Mar 30, 2026), per [Macrotrends](https://www.macrotrends.net/3229/us-high-yield-bond-spread). Macrotrends shows 3.39 for Nov 12, which disagrees with FRED's 3.20, so I don't trust its daily numbers.

**Typical daily moves:** recently about 0.05 to 0.18 pp, for example 3.26 to 3.44 between Oct 29 and Oct 30.

**Statistical baseline for Dec 4** (from 14-trading-day changes since 2005, recent years weighted double):

| Percentile | p5 | p10 | p25 | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Value (pp) | 2.86 | 2.95 | 3.09 | 3.20 | 3.32 | 3.50 | 3.62 |

**Seasonal comparison, mid-November to Dec 4:**

| Year | Mid-Nov value | Dec 4 value | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 3.09 (Nov 13) | 2.88 | -0.21 |
| 2024 | 2.64 (Nov 13) | 2.66 | +0.02 |
| 2023 | 3.92 (Nov 14) | 3.80 | -0.12 |

- In all three years, spreads were flat or tighter by early December.
- This year's level (3.23) is above 2024 and 2025 and below 2023. Unlike those years, it comes after a fresh widening.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on the HY OAS itself (Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold), and no published expert point forecast for early December.
- Related markets on Treasury yields, as of 2026-11-16:
  - Polymarket gives about 46% that the 10-year yield reaches 5.21% in November and about 9% that it reaches 5.5% before 2027.
  - Kalshi gives about 52% that the 30-year yield reaches 5.53% by Nov 30.
  - Kalshi gives about 51% that the 2-year yield reaches 4.92% this month.
  - Overall, these markets expect rates to stay high, which a Hartnett-style view treats as bad for risk assets.

## 6. Upcoming events before Dec 4
- 2026-11-17: Nvidia earnings. This is a key test for spreads on AI and data-center bonds. FRED also updates that day.
- This week: the Fed publishes its October meeting minutes (exact date not confirmed).
- 2026-11-26: US Thanksgiving holiday. Nov 27 is likely an early bond-market close with thin trading. If FRED shows no Dec 4 value, the most recent earlier value in the period is used.
- Likely 2026-12-04: the November jobs report, released on the resolution day itself (date not verified).
- After resolution: the Fed meets Dec 8 to 9, with about 85% odds of a hike reported in late October (no November odds found), and November CPI comes out Dec 10. Market positioning ahead of these could affect spreads before Dec 4.
- Ongoing risks: Treasury yield volatility (10-year above 5.1%) and further stress in CCC and single-B bonds.

## 4. Base rates
- The code baseline for 12-04, based on 14-trading-day changes since 2005, gives: p5 2.86, p10 2.95, p25 3.09, p50 3.20, p75 3.32, p90 3.50, p95 3.62.
- Recent swings are large. Single days have moved +18bp (10-30), +16bp (11-05), -12bp (10-27) and -10bp (11-12). Over the past 7 weeks the spread has ranged from 3.03 to 3.48.
- The previous 2026 peak was 3.46 on 03-30. It fell to 2.90 by 04-09, about 56bp in 8 trading days.
- Seasonality, mid-November to Dec 4 in recent years:
  - 2023: 3.92 (11-14) → 3.80 (12-04), down 12bp.
  - 2024: 2.64 (11-13) → 2.66 (12-04), up 2bp.
  - 2025: 3.09 (11-13) → 2.88 (12-04), down 21bp. It peaked at 3.20 on 11-18 before tightening through Thanksgiving.
  - In 2 of these 3 years the spread tightened into early December. The 2026 level of 3.23 is above 2024 and 2025 but below 2023.
- FRED usually publishes values for Thanksgiving and the day after (for example 2025-11-27: 3.00). [govspending CSV](https://govspending.org/api/export/fred/BAMLH0A0HYM2.csv)

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The outcome is the first FRED value published for Friday Dec 4, 2026. That is about 14 trading days after the last data point and about 2.5 weeks from today, Nov 16. It will be known around Dec 4 to 7.

(b) **Latest known value:** 3.23 pp on Nov 13, 2026, from FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2. It was 3.20 on Nov 12, and the recent peak was 3.48 on Nov 5.

(c) **If nothing changes:** about 3.23.

(d) **If the current trend continues:** The short-term trend since Nov 5 is tightening of roughly 0.25 pp, which would point to about 3.0 to 3.1. The trend since late September is widening, from about 2.7 to 3.2-3.4, which would point to about 3.4 to 3.5. Netting these out gives little directional signal.

(e) **Historical variation:** The empirical 14-trading-day changes give a 5% to 95% range of about -0.37 to +0.39 pp around the current level, with a slight right skew. Daily moves recently have been 0.05 to 0.18 pp, so the environment is more volatile than usual. That argues for somewhat wider tails, especially on the upside.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:**
- There is no direct market on this spread.
- Rates markets expect yields to stay high, with the 10-year around 5.15% and a likely Fed hike in December. Hartnett is defensive.
- AI and data-center credit stress has widened single-B spreads.
- Seasonality runs the other way: from mid-November to early December, spreads were flat or tighter in each of the last three years.
